original_question: For functions with mixed smoothness on the d-torus, specifically the space H_d^{k,mix}(T^d), independent uniformly distributed sample points are known to be optimal for the Monte Carlo error and optimal up to a logarithmic factor for the uniform error, which also yields logarithmic-factor optimality for integration. Can that logarithmic loss be removed for uniformly distributed samples, as happens in the isotropic-smoothness setting?
target_in_paper: Section 5 ("iid Information"), Remark 10: the open problem asking whether the logarithmic loss for independent uniformly distributed samples on H^{k,mix}(T^d) can be avoided, after the paper notes known results for L2-approximation and the induced logarithmic-factor statements for integration. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2307.06787))
correct_elements: Your draft already captures the right setting (mixed smoothness on the d-torus), the restriction to independent uniformly distributed sample points, the distinction between Monte Carlo error and uniform error, the fact that the approximation results imply corresponding logarithmic-factor statements for integration, and the comparison with the isotropic-smoothness case. So it is very close to the paper’s actual open problem. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2307.06787))
missing_details: The paper formulates the mixed-smoothness issue first for L2-approximation (sampling recovery) on the Hilbert space H^{k,mix}(T^d); integration is mentioned only as a consequence, not as the primary standalone problem. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2307.06787))
It should explicitly say iid uniformly distributed points on T^d, not merely uniformly distributed points. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2307.06787))

The benchmark behind "optimal" is the best asymptotic order achievable with optimally chosen sampling points, not just the existence of some good reconstruction method. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2307.06787))

The paper’s Monte Carlo error and uniform error are different criteria: the Monte Carlo error takes the supremum over the unit ball outside the expectation, while the uniform error places the expectation outside that supremum. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2307.06787))

To be fully stand-alone, the question should make clear that the issue is asymptotic in the sample size n for a fixed space H^{k,mix}(T^d), rather than an iid tractability question in the sense of the separate open problem stated immediately afterward. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2307.06787))

The paper does not state an explicit conjectured rate or logarithmic exponent here; it asks only whether the presently known logarithmic loss can be removed. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2307.06787))

No ambient field, homogeneity, degree, or nilpotency conditions are relevant here; the hidden assumptions are instead the sampling model, the target norm L2(T^d), and the precise error criterion. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2307.06787))
refined_question: For fixed d and k, let H^{k,mix}(T^d) be the Hilbert space of periodic functions of dominating mixed smoothness k on the d-torus, and let P_n = {X_1, ..., X_n} with X_1, ..., X_n iid and uniformly distributed on T^d. For the sampling recovery problem id: H^{k,mix}(T^d) -> L2(T^d), define the Monte Carlo error of an algorithm A based on P_n by sup_{||f||_{H^{k,mix}} <= 1} E ||f - A(f|_{P_n})||_{L2(T^d)} and the uniform error by E sup_{||f||_{H^{k,mix}} <= 1} ||f - A(f|_{P_n})||_{L2(T^d)}. It is known that iid uniform samples are asymptotically optimal for the Monte Carlo error and only optimal up to a logarithmic factor for the uniform error. Can this logarithmic factor be eliminated, i.e. do iid uniformly distributed samples achieve the same asymptotic order for the uniform error as optimally chosen sampling points? In particular, can one thereby remove the corresponding logarithmic loss for numerical integration on H^{k,mix}(T^d) as well? ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2307.06787))
justification: The draft is not targeting the lower-bound conjecture from Section 4 or the general iid-tractability question that follows; it is targeting the sentence in Remark 10 of Section 5. That remark explicitly narrows the discussion to L2-approximation on H^{k,mix}(T^d), states the known optimality for Monte Carlo error and only logarithmic-factor optimality for uniform error, notes the resulting implication for integration, and then poses the open question whether the logarithmic loss can be avoided for uniformly distributed samples, as in isotropic smoothness. The surrounding Section 5 discussion supplies the definitions of the Monte Carlo and uniform error criteria and explains the benchmark against optimally chosen sampling points. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2307.06787))
